correctness.rationale: C PASS: Explicit Fourier inversion for the Binomial(h,p) residue distribution modulo three yields d_h=(2/3)r^h max_k |cos(hθ-2πk/3)|. The exact change x=θ−π/3 gives r=1/(2cos x), x in [−π/3,π/3], p=1/2+tan x/(2sqrt3). The phase maximum is bounded below by sqrt3/2, with equality at |hx|=π/6; for |x|≥π/(6h), the denominator 2^h cos(x)^h yields a strict global bound except at ±π/(6h). For 0<|x|<π/(6h), logarithmic derivative h(tan x−tan(hx))<0. Thus precisely two minima for every h>=2. A direct one-step computation establishes [1/3,2/3]; eigenvalue modulus minimizes uniquely at p=1/2; strict ratio and asymptotics use elementary expansion. Independently reconstructed the binomial law and confirmed 9009 grid comparisons across 9 horizons; grid does not prove global optimization.

value.rationale: V PASS: The exact all-horizon optimizer distinguishes finite-time distributional error from an asymptotic eigenvalue criterion in the smallest directed nonreversible cycle; the optimal tuning shift and persistent relative advantage are natural algorithmic quantities, not a single arbitrary numerical example.

final_claim: For every integer h>=2, the lazy clockwise three-cycle P_p=(1-p)I+pS has exactly two finite-horizon TV minimizers p=1/2 ± tan(pi/(6h))/(2sqrt(3)); the minimum is sqrt(3)sec(pi/(6h))^h/(3*2^h); for h=1 the entire interval [1/3,2/3] minimizes.
limitations: The h=1 minimizer is a continuum, not two points; p=0,1 allowed but not ergodic; no uniform optimum outside this one-parameter directed cycle.
